ABSTRACT

In this paper, a novel semisupervised algorithm is proposed

with spatial similarity for classi ﬁ cation of hyperspectral data

based on the transductive support vector machines algorithm.

The proposed method exploits the characteristic of the hyper-

spectral data, in which spatially nearby points are likely to

belong to the same class. To utilize this assumption, a novel

transductive support vector machines algorithm is proposed.

Experimental tests are performed on two hyperspectral data

sets. The results show that the proposed algorithm obtains

higher classi ﬁ cation accuracies.

Index Terms—Image classi ﬁ cation, kernel methods,

transductive support vector machines, spatial similarity

1. INTRODUCTION

Earth observation images by satellite sensors provide diverse

information for environmental monitoring services. In order

to make the images usable for monitoring purposes, super-

vised classi ﬁ cation methods are mainly utilized due to their

ability to make more accurate classi ﬁ cation results. Note that

the success of supervised classi ﬁ cation methods depends on

the quantity and quality of labeled samples. Nevertheless, the

process of collecting training samples is time-consuming and

expensive in most cases. To avoid a selection of too many

training samples, one way is to utilize the information con-

tained in the massive unlabeled samples. The method is called

semisupervised learning (SSL) method [1].

SSL is a very active ﬁ eld of machine learning and has at-

tracted wide research interests in remote sensing image classi-

ﬁ cation. Among the most successful SSL methods, the Trans-

ductive Support Vector Machines (TSVM) [2] try to max-

imize the margin for both labeled and semilabled samples,

which are obtained based on the current classi ﬁ cation hyper-

planes. In [3], the information c ontained in labeled samples is

propagated to their neighbors via graphs until the whole im-

age obtains a global steady state. In [4], the SVM decision

Despite their good performances and simplicity, these

methods seldom consider spatial characteristics of remote

sensing images. Remote sensing images are spatially contin-

uous due to the fact that the land cover types in the Earth are

continuous. Hence, if one pixel belongs to one land cover

type, e.g., cropland, it is plausible that the spatially nearby

pixels also belong to cropland without other information.

Since SSL methods try their best to exploit the unlabeled

samples to improve the classi ﬁ cation model, they should also

utilize this intuitive assumption.

In this paper, a novel transductive SVM is proposed based

on the above idea. The structure of this paper is organized

as follows: Section 2 presents the proposed algorithm, after

brie ﬂ y describing the TSVM algorithm; Section 3 presents

two hyperspectral data sets used and experimental results and

discussions; and Section 4 ﬁ nally draws the conclusion of this

work.

2.2. Proposed TSVM

On the basis of the standard theoretical approach of the

TSVM, the proposed TSVM gives a novel de ﬁ nition of trans-

ductive samples. The novel transductive samples are intro-

duced according to observations of remotely sensed images.

As stated above, pixels nearby are more likely to belong to

the same class, and the spatial distance can be considered as

a simple measure of spatial consistency.

2.2.1. Selection of Transductive Samples

Different from the method in [2], the proposed criterion ran-

domly selects the unlabeled samples. Then query the nearest

labeled sample for each unlabeled sample based on Euclidean

distance d ul (i.e., the distance between the unlabeled sample

x∗

Euclidean distances with their n earest labeled samples are s-

maller than a ﬁ xed threshold, are selected as transductive sam-

ples. The same labels are given the transductive samples as

those of their nearest labeled samples.

3.3. Results and Discussions

The classi ﬁ cation results for the two data sets are displayed in

Fig. 1 and Fig. 2, respectively. The mean overall accuracy im-

provement by the proposed algorithm is 2.9% for the KSC da-

ta set, and an improvement of 5.2% is obtained for the Indian

Pine data set. It convinces that the proposed algorithm is ef-

fective, even in the extreme case where transductive samples

are randomly selected. It can seen from the two ﬁ gures, with

training samples increase, the improvement in classi ﬁ cation

accuracy decreases. It can be explained by that: with more

training samples, the classi ﬁ cation model will be more accu-

rate, and the spatially randomly transductive samples provide

less information to the classi ﬁ cation model.

Note that the improvement on classi ﬁ cation accuracy by

the proposed algorithm is limited with respect to the standard

SVM for both the two data sets. The main reason is that the

transductive samples in the proposed algorithm are randomly

selected by reinforcing a spatial distance constraint. Besides,

the labeling process for the transductive samples is very sim-

ple, lacking in consideration o f the predicted labels based on

the obtained classi ﬁ cation model. More elaborated process of

selecting transductive samples should consider the expected

accurate labeling and the informativeness of unlabeled sam-

ples, as in [2].

in a large quantities of unlabeled samples. The proposed algo-

rithm simply uses the intuitive assumption in remote sensing

images: spatial nearby pixels are more related in their true

land cover types. Experimental tests on two hyperspectral

data sets demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed algo-

Article

  * Jan 2023

  * Junyuan Ding
  * Wei Wei
  * Lei Zhang

Due to the huge number of trainable parameters, deep learning based hyperspectral image(HSI) classification method frequently struggle to achieve satisfactory accuracy when providing small amount of labeled training samples. This study proposes a novel few-shot transfer learning based HSI classification method, which can exploit samples from multiple other HSI datasets(termed as multi-source domain) to address the issues of limited labeled samples in target domain. For this purpose, we first construct a feature extractor utilizing both convolution neural network (CNN) and transformer. Specifically, CNN extracts features of HSI in spatial domain, while transformer is used to capture both global and local features within spectral domain. Since the constructed feature extractor is trained on multiple HSIs from source domain, it has a good generalization ability. To alleviate these problems, the method incorporates three ingredients, respectively. First, being a kernel-based method, it combats the curse of dimensionality efficiently. Second, following a semi-supervised approach, it exploits the wealth of unlabeled samples in the image, and naturally gives relative importance to the labeled ones through a graph-based methodology. Finally, it incorporates contextual information through a full family of composite kernels. Noting that the graph method relies on inverting a huge kernel matrix formed by both labeled and unlabeled samples, we originally introduce the Nystro umlm method in the formulation to speed up the classification process. The presented semi-supervised-graph-based method is compared to state-of-the-art support vector machines in the classification of hyperspectral data. The proposed method produces better classification maps, which capture the intrinsic structure collectively revealed by labeled and unlabeled points. Good and stable accuracy is produced in ill-posed classification problems (high dimensional spaces and low number of labeled samples). 
Article

  * Nov 2006

  * Mikhail Belkin
  * Partha Niyogi
  * Vikas Sindhwani

We propose a family of learning algorithms based on a new form of regularization that allows us to exploit the geometry of the marginal distribution. We focus on a semi-supervised framework that incorporates labeled and unlabeled data in a general-purpose learner. Some transductive graph learning algorithms and standard methods including Support Vector Machines and Regularized Least Squares can be obtained as special cases. We utilize properties of Reproducing Kernel Hilbert spaces to prove new Representer theorems that provide theoretical basis for the algorithms. As a result (in contrast to purely graph-based approaches) we obtain a natural out-of-sample extension to novel examples and so are able to handle both transductive and truly semi-supervised settings. We present experimental evidence suggesting that our semi-supervised algorithms are able to use unlabeled data effectively. Finally we have a brief discuss ion of unsupervised and fully supervised learning within our general framework.
